COVID-19 Impact & Recovery
October 2022 Update
Damian Betebenner— Center for Assessment

Indiana DOE Assessment TAC

October 13th, 2022

Impact & Recovery
• Recall:
• Academic impact is analogous to a headwind, decreasing the rate of student learning
(deceleration) which, in turn leads to lower attainment
• Academic recovery is analogous to a tailwind, increasing the rate of student learning
(acceleration) which, in turn leads to higher attainment
• 2019 to 2021, under the strong presumption that educational disruptions between spring 2020 to
spring 2021 led to learning deceleration, we examined academic impact
• 2021 to 2022, under the assumption/desire that student education approximating normal, led to
learning stabilization/recovery, we examined academic recovery.
• Examination of academic impact/recovery are opposite sides of the same coin and utilize the same
analytics.
• It is important to note that any meaningful discussion about recovery presumes an understanding
of the magnitude of impact.

Impact & Recovery
• We investigate impact/recovery in two ways:
• Change in same grade/same cohort attainment: We examine equi-percentile change in
attainment.
• Change in student growth: We examine change in baseline student growth (SGPs) utilizing
coefficient matrices derived from pre-pandemic cohorts of students. 2017 to 2019 growth for
2019 to 2021
• As Rich pointed out at the last TAC meeting, attainment is to odometer as growth is to
speedometer.
• Across multiple states the correlation (grades/content area/state) between these two measures of
impact are 0.81.
• Low participation the largest cause of outliers between the two indicators
• We utilize change in student growth for grades/cohorts with that quantity and change in
attainment (mapped to change in student growth) for grades/cohorts that don’t.

2019 to 2021: Impact
• ELA
• Decreases in percent proficient ranged from upper single digits in lower grades to lower single
digits in higher grades.
• Median (baseline) SGPs ranged from upper 30s to lower 40s
• Impacts were categorized as moderate
• Mathematics
• Decreases in percent proficient was in the lower teens
• Median (baseline) SGPs ranged from the low to mid 30s.
• Impacts were categorized as large
• Moderate, large, and severe impacts likely require multiple years of above average (pre-pandemic)
growth to recover to where students would have been had the pandemic not occurred.

Nationwide
• We are in the middle of tabulating results for about a dozen states on the extent
of recovery occurring
• Overall, most states are stabilizing or stabilizing bordering on deterioration. There
is at least one state whose results indicate rates of learning that would lead to
student recovery
• I have seen examples from several states (some in great detail) which make me
question whether the psychometrics (e.g., equating/linking) are holding up over
the course of the pandemic.
• Analyses such as these will require a stable scale going forward.

Secondary Analyses:
Impact & Recovery
• Many states and research organizations are interested in examining student assessment data
to examine student impact/recovery in relation to pandemic mitigation efforts and pandemic
academic recovery efforts.
• This interest is particularly acute due to the large amounts of money being directed at
schools/districts to help with student academic recovery.
• Return on investment (ROI) analyses have been discussed with several states including
Indiana.
• ROI analyses present numerous significant challenges including:
• Inconsistent terminology used by schools/corporations/state (e.g., high-dosage tutoring)
• Funding sources either not detailed or coming from multiple sources
• Fidelity of implementation may vary greatly across sites

Exemplar Schools: Impact & Recovery
• ROI discussions in Indiana focused on two areas:
• Identifying outlier schools based upon impact/recovery patterns and doing in-depth
follow-up interviews to determine what, if any, activities these schools engaged in.
That is, switch from return on investment to return on activities. (post hoc
investigation)
• Schools receiving 1008 funding (a priori investigation)
• We have begun both of these analyses.
• For the outlier schools We investigated schools along two dimensions:
• Academic Impact (2019 to 2021 decrease in student learning)
• Academic Recovery (2021 to 2022 increase in student learning relative to pre-
pandemic 2018-2019 learning)

1008 Schools
• Indiana’s House Bill 1008, the student learning recovery grant program, put forth
up to $150,000,000 to establish:
• Student learning recovery grant program
• Student learning recovery grant program fund
• Entities eligible to receive grant money had to develop and submit a student
learning acceleration plan.
• Due to the large sums of money being devoted to such programs together with
the unprecedented academic situation students currently face, Indiana is keenly
interested in understanding whether recovery programs being implemented are
successful.

1008 Schools
• We have just begun investigating impact associated with 1008 schools.
• 1008 participation began summer 2021.
• Initially we investigated results for schools in Marion County (includes
Indianapolis)
• Data from Marion County schools included student level participation indicating
total minutes of participation in four categories: ELA, Mathematics, CCR (Career/
College Readiness), and Other as well as Total Minutes
• Additional statewide data was also just received. Quality of the data varies greatly
from corporation to corporation.
